title: Cyrus and the Border
premise: Isandro Villalobos, a gifted interpreter with a forged past, has spent years translating for peace delegations while keeping one foot ready to flee. When a burner phone rings with the voice of his presumed-dead brother Mateo—now entangled with an assassin hired to sabotage the talks—he must choose between the duty that shields him and the family that betrayed him. As he smuggles evidence of a manufactured ceasefire violation past three intelligence services and a killer named Voss, Isandro finds unexpected belonging with delegation aide Priya Raghavan and her ragtag security detail. In the end, he trades his invisibility for testimony, exposing the plot minutes before Frankfurt markets open, and chooses to stay—unpacked, unmasked, and finally home.
about_author: U. M. Dunmore is the pen name of a former conference interpreter who spent a decade in negotiation rooms across three continents before turning to fiction. They write thrillers about people whose professions demand silence.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag by the Door
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Arriving in Geneva for the Meridian Accords, he rehearses his cover story and checks his packed bag out of habit. A quiet scene establishing his double life: fluent in five languages, honest in none. Emotional beat: the loneliness of permanent readiness, interrupted when an unknown number calls his burner—the voice is unmistakably Mateo's.

chapters.title: A Voice from the Drowned Year
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, flashback braided into present. Mateo warns him to walk away from the Accords before hanging up on a dead man's number. Isandro verifies the call was real, then lies smoothly to delegation chief Ambassador Okafor about why he's shaken. Emotional beat: grief reopening; the first crack in his polished lie as Priya notices he's lying badly.

chapters.title: Terms of Art
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. She audits the translation team after a mistranslation nearly derails a session and finds Isandro's file too clean. Their wary working alliance forms over late-night document review. Meanwhile a delegate's aide is found dead in the lake—an apparent suicide. Emotional beat: two guarded people recognizing each other's masks, attraction kindling under professional suspicion.

chapters.title: What the Interpreter Heard
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Reviewing session recordings, he catches a phrase spoken off-mic in Farsi that doesn't match the official transcript—a planted admission of a border incursion scheduled to look like the other side's doing. He pockets the recording instead of reporting it. Emotional beat: the vertigo of holding truth that could save or destroy him, and the pull toward Priya making silence harder.

chapters.title: Voss
chapters.summary: Voss's POV, cold and procedural. The assassin cleans up the dead aide's trail and identifies the recording's existence through hotel keycard data. He notes Isandro as a thread to cut but delays, ordered to let the talks proceed until markets open Monday. Emotional beat: chilling competence; the reader sees the trap closing while Isandro feels only momentum.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Lie
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. He tries to pass the recording to Okafor and is rebuffed—Okafor already suspects the talks are theater but needs Isandro silent to protect his own endgame. Isandro realizes every government at the table wants the failure. He tells Priya everything except his real name. Emotional beat: betrayal compounding; love against duty crystallizes as Priya chooses to help anyway.

chapters.title: The Border Crossing
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The pair go off-book, driving evidence to a French journalist via back roads. A checkpoint stop nearly ends them; Isandro talks them through in three languages, improvising identities with terrifying fluency. Found family solidifies: the delegation's gruff driver, Tomas, covers their absence without being asked. Emotional beat: belonging discovered mid-flight—for the first time, someone has his back.

chapters.title: Mateo's Confession
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Mateo surfaces in person, revealing he faked his death to infiltrate the saboteurs' network and that Voss reports to a private intelligence firm shorting the affected markets. Brothers argue bitterly—Mateo chose deception for duty; Isandro chose it for fear. Emotional beat: forgiveness offered but not yet accepted; Mateo gives Isandro the firm's ledger and a warning: Voss knows about Priya.

chapters.title: Sunday Night
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, ticking-clock structure. Voss takes Priya hostage in the delegation residence to force the recording's surrender; Isandro walks into the trap carrying the ledger instead, negotiating in the assassin's own mother tongue—a language Voss thought no one there spoke. Okafor, moved at last, unlocks the secure channel. Emotional beat: climax of nerve; Isandro stops translating others' words and finally speaks his own truth aloud.

chapters.title: Markets Open in Frankfurt
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. At 8:59 a.m., the evidence hits the wire: the incursion footage, the ledger, Isandro's sworn statement naming himself. Talks collapse—but honestly—and the short positions burn. Voss vanishes; Mateo surrenders to prosecutors with Isandro promising to testify as family, not informant. Final scene: Isandro unpacks the go-bag, item by item, in Priya's kitchen. Emotional beat: resolution—duty redefined as truth-telling, belonging chosen over escape.
